title: Study finds agent skills can leak credentials through ordinary debug output
friendlyTitle: Some AI agent skills may expose passwords and access keys
summary: Researchers analysed a sample of 17,022 third-party agent skills and reported 520 affected skills with 1,708 credential-security issues. Debug logging accounted for most identified vulnerabilities because tool output can be copied into an agent’s model context.
friendlySummary: A large study found many security problems in third-party agent skills. A common issue was secret information appearing in normal debug messages that the AI could read.
whyItMatters: Installing an agent skill can grant code access to tokens, files and command output, so marketplace popularity is not a security review. Users and platform operators should isolate secrets, suppress sensitive logs, inspect skill code and revoke exposed credentials rather than relying on prompt instructions.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Check a skill before installing it and give it as little access as possible. If a secret is exposed, replace it instead of only deleting the message.
